title: App Service Deployment
description: Learn the most common ways to deploy code to Azure App Service, including ZIP deploy, run from package, Git, and GitHub Actions.

data.text: Deploying to App Service means moving your built application files from your machine or repository to the Azure-hosted environment. App Service supports several methods, from simple ZIP uploads to fully automated CI/CD pipelines.

data.title: Ways to Deploy
items: **ZIP Deploy** — Upload a ZIP file of your published app. Fast and simple for small updates.
**Run From Package** — App Service runs your app directly from a read-only ZIP. This avoids file-locking issues and makes deployments atomic.
**Local Git** — Push code directly to a Git endpoint provided by App Service.
**GitHub Actions** — A full CI/CD pipeline that builds and deploys on every commit.

data.title: Azure CLI — ZIP Deploy
data.content: Deploy a published ZIP file to an App Service app
data.code:
# Publish your app first (example for .NET)
dotnet publish --configuration Release --output ./publish
Compress-Archive -Path ./publish/* -DestinationPath ./app.zip

# Deploy the ZIP to App Service
az webapp deployment source config-zip \
  --resource-group MyResourceGroup \
  --name MyWebApp \
  --src ./app.zip

data.text: Run From Package mounts your deployment ZIP as a read-only drive. This prevents file-locking issues during restarts and makes your deployment more predictable. Most modern frameworks support publishing directly to a ZIP.

data.title: Azure CLI — Run From Package
data.content: Enable Run From Package using an app setting
data.code:
# Upload your ZIP to a storage account first, then set the app setting
az webapp config appsettings set \
  --resource-group MyResourceGroup \
  --name MyWebApp \
  --settings WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE="https://myaccount.blob.core.windows.net/deploy/app.zip"

data.text: GitHub Actions is the recommended approach for production apps. It builds your code, runs tests, and deploys to App Service automatically. The Azure/login and Azure/webapps-deploy actions handle the heavy lifting.

data.title: Benefits of GitHub Actions
items: Automated builds and tests before deployment
Deployment history and rollback in GitHub
Works with staging slots for safer releases

data.title: Start with ZIP Deploy
data.text: If you are new to App Service, try ZIP deploy first. It is the simplest method and works well for manual updates and learning.

terms.definition: An App Service deployment method that uploads a ZIP archive of your published application.
A deployment mode where App Service runs the app from a read-only ZIP file, avoiding file-locking issues.
GitHub's CI/CD platform that can automatically build and deploy your app to Azure.
An automated process that deploys code changes after they pass tests.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: ZIP Deploy is fast and easy for manual updates.
Run From Package is the recommended production deployment mode.
GitHub Actions provides automated CI/CD without extra servers.
Choose the method that fits your workflow: manual ZIP for quick tests, Actions for production.
data.takeaway: Deploying to App Service is straightforward once you choose the right method for your team.
